prompt:
You describe a pinout or package drawing from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. The package or module, the view (top or bottom) and where pin 1 is, if shown.
2. Every pin as "number: name", in pin order. Do not skip pins; if a pin number or name is unreadable, say so.
3. Every dimension with its unit and tolerance, if shown.

Figure type: pinout or package drawing
Section: VQFN - 1.0 mm max height
Caption: none
Text inside the figure (exact, from the PDF text layer): 20X (0.7) | 20X (0.24) | 16X (0.5) | (3.7) | (3.7) | (0.6) TYP | (0.6) TYP | 4X ( 1) | (R0.05) TYP | SYMM | SYMM | 1 | 5 | 6 10 | 11 | 15 | 20 16 | 21
Text that mentions the figure: PLASTIC QUAD FLATPACK - NO LEAD

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".
